name: Speckle-chested Piculet
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern peru in southeastern amazonas and northwestern san martín
description: Tiny woodpecker restricted to a small area of the Andes in northern Peru. Combination of dark breast marked with white spots and heavily barred belly separate it from other piculets in the region.

name: Fawn-breasted Bowerbird
rangeDescription: New guinea and northern queensland (cape york peninsula)
description: Medium-sized bowerbird found in a diverse range of habitats across northern Cape York and New Guinea, usually in tropical moist forest but also in shrubland, parks, and gardens. Primarily grayish brown with subtle orange wash in belly, diffuse streaking in throat and breast.

name: Helmeted Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, and northern amazonian brazil
description: Tiny flycatcher; common and widespread, but heard far more often than seen. When seen well, note pale eye and elongated crown feathers, giving this bird a hammer-headed appearance.

name: Ash-throated Antwren
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of north-central peru (san martín)
description: Rare antwren restricted to a small area of the eastern Andes in northern Peru. Note the black cap, striped face, white wingbars, and lack of rufous in the wing.

name: Giant Wood-Rail
rangeDescription: Marshes of southeastern brazil to paraguay, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Easy to recognize by its gigantic size. Note the rusty neck and belly that help to distinguish it from similar smaller wood-rails.

name: Ruddy Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southeastern venezuela and northern brazil (cerro uei-tepui in roraima)
description: A small, charismatic bird of tepui highland forests. Note orange-rufous face and breast, short tail, and bold wing bars.

name: Rennell White-eye
rangeDescription: Rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Body and head entirely uniform olive-green. Eye black with a thin bluish ring.

name: Crimson-hooded Myzomela
rangeDescription: Wetar (lesser sundas)
description: A small gray honeyeater with a downcurved bill, a white belly, and a contrasting red head and rump. Males show more red on head than females; red extends to breast on male birds from Wetar, confined to throat in Alor.

name: Pacific Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of western ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Tiny, sparrow-sized parrot of lowlands and foothills in western Ecuador, western Peru, and far southwestern Colombia. Most common in dry habitats such as desert and deciduous forest, but has spread into humid areas in response to deforestation.

name: Tanganyika Masked-Weaver
rangeDescription: Swamps of southwestern tanzania (karema to rukwa) and zambia
description: A typical red-eyed masked-weaver with a plain olive-green back and pink-brown legs. The breeding male has a black face mask extending midway up the forehead, surrounded by a strong burnt-orange wash that spreads to the breast and flanks.

name: Plain Parakeet
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (bahia and southern goiás to rio grande do sul)
description: Small and uniformly green parakeet with a long pointed tail and a pinkish bill and feet. In flight, the blue outer wing feathers and tail tips are visible.

name: Cabanis's Wren
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (oaxaca) southward on the pacific slope to northwestern costa rica; locally on the caribbean slope from southern mexico (chiapas) to honduras
description: Small, skulking wren of foothills and lowlands in southern Mexico and Central America. Found in forest edges, second-growth thickets, and brushy fields with cane grass.

name: Blacksmith Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds southernmost brazil (north to paraná), northeastern argentina, and southeastern paraguay; winters northward to south-central brazil (northward to mato grosso and goiás)
description: A distinctive gray thrush found in lowlands of southeast Brazil and Paraguay. Males are gray-brown above and pale grayish below with a conspicuous streaked white throat, yellow bill, and yellow feet.

name: Black Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off california and baja california; ranges to peru
description: Large, dark, angular storm-petrel with a deeply notched tail. Looks long-necked and large-billed.

name: Swainson's Hawk
rangeDescription: Western north america; winters to northern argentina, southern brazil, and paraguay
description: Longer-winged than Red-tailed Hawk, but otherwise the same size. Found in prairies and agricultural regions of western U.S.

name: Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (mindoro)
description: A small bird of lowland and foothill forest and more open wooded areas on Mindoro, slightly glossy black with a white belly and sides of the chest and with red patches on the throat, upper back, and in a stripe from the center of the chest down the belly. Note the fairly long, thin, slightly curved bill.

name: Gray Wren-Warbler
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan, ethiopia, somalia, northeastern uganda, kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: A very dark, long-tailed warbler of dry country. Blackish-gray overall with a reddish eye and white tips to the tail.

name: Rand's Warbler
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Plain, warbler-like tetraka with a bold white eye-stripe. Madagascar endemic that is found in low and middle-elevation rainforest.

name: Mees's Nightjar
rangeDescription: Lesser sundas (sumba and flores)
description: A large, long-tailed nightjar from Sumba and Flores. Shows bold white patches in tail and wings in flight.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Sao Tome Ibis
rangeDescription: São tomé island (gulf of guinea)
description: Very small, dark forest-dwelling ibis. Note the dark blue bare skin on the face, the ragged crest, and the glossy green shoulders.
